comments.body:
🤖 Bounded paired cost update: local candidate `fbb1fc8378601e0346d00d186809f10d1ad0360d` satisfies the fixed-route FP32-combine contract, but it was slower than #276 parent `0c213586b5491b8046ca7780e965c4b26dc6a2a2` on every one of eight paired H100s and used more HBM at the affected combine boundary. This was predeclared as estimate-only, so I am not assigning a practical-regression threshold after seeing the result.

## Local correctness

The arms used byte-identical BF16 state, hidden inputs, fixed expert IDs, combine weights, and cotangent. Expert-output times weight multiplication remained BF16; only the running-sum dtype differed. Independent fixed-slot-order FP32 and FP64 reductions consumed the path's BF16 weighted summands rather than calling either product combine implementation.

- Parent eager and grouped outputs each differed from the FP32 reference in `4,096 / 524,288` elements, with maximum absolute error `0.015625`.
- Candidate eager and grouped outputs were bitwise equal to the FP32 reference and to the BF16-cast FP64 reference: zero output failures and zero maximum error.
- Against the independent uncast FP64 accumulator, the returned BF16 output's maximum/mean error fell from parent `0.01171875 / 0.000091552734375` to candidate `0.00390625 / 0.000030517578125`.
- Candidate eager and grouped outputs were bitwise equal. All combine-weight, hidden, expert-gate, up, and down gradient checks passed the frozen `rtol=0.08, atol=0.0001` rule with zero failures. The eager/grouped hidden-gradient maximum difference was `2.384185791015625e-7`; the other four gradient targets were bitwise equal.
- The first four required gates passed at their stated scope, including exact candidate output/gradient checks and discrimination of the parent's known BF16 running-sum error. Post-run review found that the fifth gate's "pre-cast" label overstated its implementation: its true boolean compared the returned BF16 product output with the independent uncast FP64 accumulator. The product's internal pre-final-cast FP32 accumulator was not captured, so I am not making a direct product pre-cast claim. The frozen packet and reader are unchanged.

The correctness fixture was 4,096 tokens, hidden 128, expert intermediate 64, five experts, top-4.

## Paired H100 measurement

The measured fixture used the real expert shape: 8,192 tokens, hidden 2,560, expert intermediate 1,280, 256 experts, top-4. Routes were fixed outside the router and perfectly balanced at 128 rows per expert. Each physical GPU ran both arms twice in alternating order; each fresh process performed five warmups and twenty measured iterations, for 40 samples per arm/GPU. CUDA events enclosed forward and backward with synchronized completion. Setup and gradient clearing were outside the timed region.

For HBM accounting, the frozen protocol emptied the allocator cache after warmup. The first retained iteration in each process therefore included post-empty-cache allocations and was visibly slower than the other 19. All samples were retained. Each arm had two such high samples in its 40-sample per-GPU pool, so neither determined the reported median; the median came from the stable post-allocation iterations.

The primary boundary called the hash-pinned product `_forward_grouped` with routing fixed: route sorting, routed-input construction, grouped expert projections, BF16 weighting, combine, and backward. It does not include the router. The product has no standalone combine callable, so the isolated combine boundary was a driver implementation of the same affected operations.

| GPU | Parent full F+B ms | Candidate full F+B ms | Delta ms | Ratio |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 0 | 13.978896 | 14.481008 | +0.502112 | 1.035919 |
| 1 | 13.955856 | 14.496912 | +0.541056 | 1.038769 |
| 2 | 13.995952 | 14.494256 | +0.498303 | 1.035603 |
| 3 | 13.961344 | 14.502992 | +0.541648 | 1.038796 |
| 4 | 13.992480 | 14.513088 | +0.520608 | 1.037206 |
| 5 | 13.967488 | 14.501280 | +0.533792 | 1.038217 |
| 6 | 14.001856 | 14.543184 | +0.541328 | 1.038661 |
| 7 | 13.986448 | 14.532112 | +0.545664 | 1.039014 |

Across the eight paired GPU medians:

- Full-block forward + backward: candidate-parent median `+0.537424` ms, range `+0.498303` to `+0.545664` ms; median ratio `1.038439`, range `1.035603` to `1.039014`.
- Full-block forward alone: median `+0.212600` ms; ratio `1.046230`. Backward alone: median `+0.310968` ms; ratio `1.033177`.
- Complete affected combine forward + backward: median `+0.531640` ms, range `+0.523488` to `+0.543248` ms; median ratio `1.340920`, range `1.335353` to `1.348955`.
- Combine forward alone: median `+0.217800` ms; ratio `1.219420`. Backward alone: median `+0.313688` ms; ratio `1.553185`.

HBM baselines, peaks, and peak-minus-baseline were identical across repetitions and GPUs within each arm:

| Boundary and arm | Baseline bytes | Peak bytes | Incremental peak bytes |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Full block, parent | 5,118,757,888 | 10,819,433,472 | 5,700,675,584 |
| Full block, candidate | 5,118,757,888 | 10,819,433,472 | 5,700,675,584 |
| Complete combine, parent | 5,622,931,456 | 6,168,322,048 | 545,390,592 |
| Complete combine, candidate | 5,622,931,456 | 6,419,914,752 | 796,983,296 |

The complete-combine incremental peak therefore increased by exactly `251,592,704` bytes on every GPU, a ratio of `1.461307`. The full-block peak delta was zero because a larger part of that boundary set both peaks; this does not show that FP32 accumulation itself has no memory cost.

## Pins, safety, and readback

Iris supplied one whole `h100-8x` node in `cw-rno2a` at interactive priority: eight H100 80GB devices, 32 CPU, 128 GiB memory, and 200 GiB ephemeral storage. The pinned runtime used Torch `2.11.0+cu129`, CUDA 12.9, driver 595.71.05, image digest `sha256:9af9a3d38f57c2ed8dfe1d6f6657a9f4a00c582ec06a5ac2af8fcddbe51da03c`, and package-inventory SHA-256 `8df26c4fa6f5bd79d25f22a9fd31bda8d4627af8083a975d1124f1b6dda84a77`.

Two dependency-preflight attempts exposed missing `ray` and then a lazy `torchtitan` import. Neither wrote a result JSON and performance did not start. The runtime was completed with the project's exact pins; only the runtime inventory and freeze timestamp changed. The fixture, numerical rules, finite schedule, driver, reader, and estimate-only verdict did not.

The successful run recorded 93 one-second memory samples. Maximum cgroup use was `25,553,707,008` bytes, below the frozen 100 GiB stop point; minimum host available memory was `2,063,631,482,880` bytes, above the 256 GiB stop point. The remote host had no swap. No worker ran on the local host. After copying and verifying the packet, the Iris holder was terminated and its Kubernetes pod was absent.

The standard-library reader passed 344 assertions and recomputed the paired summary. A local readback regenerated the JSON summary, Markdown summary, and reader stdout byte-for-byte from the copied raw packet. Raw packet SHA-256: `60e882a908643ae487b6f2f2a1c0c979a6a3d10bb9dccd97c40601c98e02526e`.

[Human-readable report, frozen protocol, raw packet, reader, and compact summaries](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/tree/40d365d661f3acc411a78b8801000a4eae964512/evidence/grug_fp32_combine_paired_20260805).

## Disposition and limits

This result does not change the controlling distributed evidence. The latest instrumented 32-H100 gate still failed `1 / 12,288` action log probabilities at rank 22, microbatch 54, model token 8010. Its last matching sampled boundary was layer-2 decoder input and its first differing sampled boundary was layer-2 post-attention hidden; the first sampled route mismatch appeared only at layer 23. The bounded causal sparse-block probe reported `no_causal_internal_divergence`. That probe neither exonerates grouped MoE across runs nor identifies attention as causal.

No live replay or distributed run was launched for this measurement. It proves only the candidate's local fixed-route accumulation contract and estimates its block-level cost on this shape. `fbb1fc8` remains off MarinSkyRL #276, the failed action-output gate remains failed, and #7903 remains unresolved.

issues.body:
## Description

Build a Zephyr pipeline that turns DOCX records in Common Crawl WARCs into Marin [`NormalizedData`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/normalize.py). Use the PDF extraction step in #7618 as a model.

Use [DocxCorpus](https://github.com/superdoc/docx-corpus) as a reference for two operations. It uses Docling to map DOCX files to text. It uses lingua for language identification (LID). Its classifiers, embeddings, storage service, API, and user interface are out of scope.

DocxCorpus reports [1,101,537 uploaded files and 736,242 classified files](https://docxcorp.us/dataset). It has extracted only a fraction of the DOCX files in Common Crawl. The Marin pipeline must read Common Crawl indexes. It must not use the DocxCorpus manifest as its source list.

Reuse the WARC range fetch and provenance fields from [`focus_crawl.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/datakit/focus_crawl.py).

### Definition of Done

- A Zephyr step reads DOCX candidates from a selected Common Crawl index. The query uses MIME and URL data.
- The step fetches each WARC record, validates the DOCX container, extracts text, and detects the language.
- The output keeps the crawl ID, source URL, WARC path, offset, length, text, and language.
- The step writes valid `NormalizedData`.
- Counters report valid files, invalid files, empty text, and extraction errors.
- Tests cover valid, malformed, empty, and multilingual DOCX fixtures.
- A sample run reports extraction yield and includes a manual text review.

issues.author: wmoss
issues.body:
#### **Context & Goal**
Currently, Zephyr data pipeline steps are defined in Python using operators like `map_step`, `flat_map_step`, and `reduce_step`. To support high-performance distributed SQL execution via DataFusion/Ballista, we want to introduce a first-class `.sql` operator in Zephyr that accepts SQL query strings or `.sql` files and executes them over dataset partitions.

---

#### **Key Considerations to Address**

* **File I/O Integration**: How does the `.sql` operator interact with loading and writing files? Is file loading and output serialization handled natively within SQL (e.g., `CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE ... LOCATION ...` and `COPY TO ...`), or handled by Zephyr's reader/writer stages?
* **Stage Boundary Isolation**: Does Zephyr always consider a `.sql` operator as a separate, distinct stage with reading and writing from GCS as its interface?
* **Execution Engine Dispatch**: How does the `.sql` operator dispatch queries between local DataFusion (for single-node execution) and the distributed Ballista cluster on Iris?
* **Metadata & Schema Propagation**: How are dataset schema validation, row counts, and output metadata passed through the `.sql` stage to downstream Zephyr operators?

---

#### **Proposed Tasks**

* [ ] **Operator API**: Define the user-facing syntax for registering `.sql` steps in Zephyr pipelines (e.g., `sql_step(...)`).
* [ ] **Execution Handler**: Implement the stage executor that bridges Zephyr task specs to DataFusion / Ballista execution contexts.
* [ ] **Integration Tests**: Add end-to-end test coverage running `.sql` stages in Zephyr pipelines over Parquet/NdJson datasets on GCS.

issues.author: ayush1298
issues.body:
🤖 Related to the evals wish-list in https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7090 (item 12). Proposing a procedurally generated, difficulty-parameterized proxy for SciCode. This issue is a design proposal only. I'd like agreement on scope and on the questions at the bottom before writing the generator.

Of the four proxy items (10–13), SciCode is the only one that is (a) graded programmatically with no judge model, (b) amenable to procedural instance generation with provably correct gold answers, and (c) validatable end-to-end on modest compute.

Briefly, why not the others yet:

- **GDPval-AA v2 (10)** — needs expert/LLM grading of open-ended deliverables plus an agentic shell+browse scaffold.
- **𝜏³-Banking (11)** — needs a user-simulator LLM per episode; sub-8B models floor on multi-turn tool use, so there is no rank signal at the scales we can cheaply validate against.
- **AA-Omniscience (13)** — its index rewards abstention, but small instruct models essentially never abstain, so the index degenerates to `2·accuracy − 1` and the calibration axis (the point of the benchmark) disappears during validation.

## The problem with SciCode as-is

SciCode is 338 subproblems from 80 main problems. At publication, the best model solved ~4.6% of main problems in the most realistic setting. A benchmark where the frontier scores single-digit and near-zero pass rates also mean near-zero information per item, so distinguishing two checkpoints needs an impractical number of samples.

The proxy's job is therefore not "SciCode but easier." It is:

> One generator and one difficulty dial such that a ~300M model sits in the sensitive band at low difficulty, a frontier model sits in the sensitive band at high difficulty, and **model ordering is preserved along the whole dial**.

## Design

### Three response modes

Same underlying item, three regimes — so one dataset serves in-loop pretraining evals *and* post-hoc generation evals:

| Mode | Format | Scoring path | Signal range |
|---|---|---|---|
| **M** | multiple-choice over candidate implementations | logprob → runs **in-loop** via the Levanter harness | ~150M–1B |
| **F** | full function given, one line masked | short generation | ~1B–7B |
| **G** | write the function from the description (SciCode-native) | generation + unit tests | 7B–frontier |

### Difficulty as a vector, not a scalar

Independent axes so we can ablate which one actually drives ranking; scalar presets `D1…D5` are fixed combinations.

| Axis | Range |
|---|---|
| `d_chain` | 1 → 6 dependent subproblems |
| `d_scaffold` | L3 formula + shapes + worked example · L2 background prose · L1 terse signature (SciCode "no background") · L0 main problem only, model decomposes |
| `d_derive` | formula given / one step away / must be derived |
| `d_numeric` | benign inputs, `rtol=1e-3` → stiff, ill-conditioned, boundary-edge, `rtol=1e-8` |
| `d_libs` | scipy allowed → numpy only → pure Python |
| `d_noise` | irrelevant prior functions injected into context |

### Metrics

- SciCode-native: **subproblem pass rate** (gold prior steps injected) and **main-problem pass rate** (all-or-nothing, model's own prior steps).
- Proxy-native: **`D50`** — difficulty level at which pass rate crosses 50%, from a logistic fit to the pass-rate-vs-difficulty curve. Scale-free and immune to both floor and ceiling effects.
- Reported separately: **format-failure rate** (unparseable output), so we can tell a genuine capability signal from markdown compliance.

### v0 task families

Mirroring 4 SciCode's categories (numerical methods/simulation / scientific calculation):

- `numcalc` — quadrature, root finding, finite-difference derivatives, Richardson extrapolation
- `ode` — Euler / RK4 / velocity-Verlet / symplectic Euler on harmonic oscillator, damped-driven pendulum, Lotka–Volterra, SIR, Kepler two-body
- `numla` — Gram–Schmidt, power iteration, Jacobi/Gauss–Seidel, Thomas tridiagonal solver, Householder QR
- `quantum1d` — finite-difference Schrödinger: build D², build H, ground state, expectation values; box / harmonic / double-well / Pöschl–Teller potentials

Some other things as well, that we can use if we were not able to get good quality samples in v0: PDE finite-difference, thin-film transfer matrices, tight-binding band structure, Ising Metropolis, Needleman–Wunsch, DFT/PSD.

### Generation

Per family, not per instance: `sample_spec(rng, difficulty)` → `reference(spec)` → `render_prompt(spec, difficulty)` → `make_tests(spec, rng)`. Test outputs are produced by running the reference, so tests are correct by construction and instances are unlimited.

**Two-implementation gate.** No instance ships unless the reference agrees with an independent source to ≥2 orders of magnitude tighter than the test tolerance — RK4 vs `solve_ivp`, harmonic-well FD Schrödinger vs analytic `E0 = ½ħω`, Gram–Schmidt vs `np.linalg.qr`, Simpson vs `scipy.integrate.quad`. This replaces scientist annotation as the correctness guarantee.

**Determinism.** Explicit seeds; pinned shape/dtype/ordering/sign/units asserted before value comparison; no wall-clock, network, or ordering-dependent structures; 5s per-test timeout; `np.allclose` with both `rtol` and `atol`; CI runs every gold solution through the grader and requires 100% pass.

**Contamination.** Randomized identifiers and parameters mean no verbatim string exists upstream. Dataset carries a canary GUID. Memorization probe: check whether a strong model reproduces the reference verbatim on a canonicalized (non-randomized) variant; if so, that family needs more randomization.


### Difficulty analysis

Difficulty analysis across four layers, cheapest first.

#### (a) Empirical difficulty curves

Pass rate vs. each axis, per model. Fit a 2-parameter logistic and report **`D50`** (difficulty at 50% pass rate) and the **slope**. Slope matters as much as location — a flat curve means the knob does nothing and the axis should be dropped or redesigned.

#### (b) Item Response Theory (2PL)

Fit `P(correct | model m, item i) = σ(a_i (θ_m − b_i))` by marginal maximum likelihood over the full model × item matrix. Three outputs, each doing real work:

- **`b_i` — item difficulty** on a common latent scale, so items from different families become directly comparable. This is what lets us claim the scalar presets D1–D5 mean the same thing across `numcalc` and `quantum1d`.
- **`a_i` — item discrimination.** The screening tool. Low-`a` items fail to separate models regardless of how hard they are, and get cut from the frozen set. This is how we avoid shipping 600 items where 200 carry the signal.
- **`θ_m` — model ability**, the natural quantity to correlate against SciCode instead of a raw pass rate.

Fitting is seconds on CPU (`py-irt`, or EM in numpy) — the constraint is having **per-item** results, not compute.

#### (c) Axis attribution

Mixed-effects logistic regression on item-level outcomes:

```
correct ~ d_chain + d_scaffold + d_derive + d_numeric + d_libs + d_noise
          + (1 | model) + (1 | family) + (1 | problem)
```

Coefficients quantify how much each knob actually moves difficulty; random effects prevent one badly-calibrated family from driving the fit. Report standardized effect sizes so axes are comparable. This is also the check against the "proxy measures numpy fluency, not science" risk — we want `d_derive` and `d_scaffold` carrying weight, not `d_libs` alone.

#### (d) Validation of the dial

Three preregistered checks:

- **Monotonicity** — pass rate non-increasing in each axis, per model.
- **Ordering stability** — model ordering preserved across ≥3 consecutive difficulty levels (Kendall τ between adjacent levels).
- **No axis inverts** — no axis where increasing difficulty *helps* some model class, which would indicate the knob measures format compliance rather than capability.

#### (e) Decomposing knowledge vs. implementation

Two mechanisms, neither requiring a judge model, both falling out of owning the reference implementation.

**Dual grading.** Score each response twice: strictly (`np.allclose`), and again under a *declared* convention group — sign/phase, scalar unit factor, eigenvalue ordering, transpose, 0-vs-1 indexing. The gap between the two scores is the **implementation tax**. A model at 30% strict and 55% tolerant knew the science and lost 25 points to conventions.

**Automatic error taxonomy.** Failures classify themselves:

| Code | Failure | Reads as |
|---|---|---|
| E0 | no parseable code | format |
| E1 | syntax / import error | format |
| E2 | runtime exception | implementation |
| E3 | wrong shape or dtype | implementation |
| E4 | right shape, values far off | **knowledge** — wrong algorithm |
| E5 | right shape, close but outside tolerance | **implementation** — convention, units, off-by-one, precision |

The **E4:E5 ratio** gives a knowledge-vs-implementation split per model and per difficulty level, at no extra cost.

**Factorial isolation.** The axes are manipulable independently, so:

- *Knowledge held out, implementation varied:* fix `d_derive = 0` (formula given verbatim), sweep `d_numeric` and convention strictness.
- *Implementation held trivial, knowledge varied:* one-line function body, no shape juggling, sweep `d_scaffold` L3 → L0 and `d_derive` 0 → 2.

Collapse in the first sweep implies implementation dominates; collapse in the second implies knowledge does. An interaction is the likely and most interesting outcome.

#### Reporting discipline

Format-failure rate (E0 + E1) is reported separately throughout, never folded into the headline. If it exceeds ~10% for a model, that model's scores are not interpretable and it is **excluded** from the correlation rather than quietly averaged in.

---

## Validation plan

We want to ensure that model rank correlation should hold w.r.t. original SciCode at substantially lower cost. Protocol:

1. **Preregister** model roster, difficulty presets, prompt template, and target metric in this issue before any correlation is computed.
2. **Dev / held-out split by family.** Tune presets on `numcalc` + `ode`; report final correlation on `numla` + `quantum1d` only.
3. **Measure the reference directly.** Run original SciCode on the roster (288 test-set subproblems, short outputs, CPU-only grading — tractable at these model sizes) rather than relying solely on published leaderboard numbers. Use published numbers as a secondary external anchor.
4. **Roster, two groups.**
   - *Scaling ladders (validity check — true order known a priori):* Qwen2.5-Instruct 0.5B→1.5B→3B→7B; Llama-3.2-1B→3.2-3B→3.1-8B
   - *Cross-family spread:* Qwen2.5-Coder-7B, DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B, Gemma-2-2B, Phi-3.5-mini, SmolLM2-1.7B, OLMo-2-7B, Qwen3-4B/8B, **Marin-8B-Instruct**
5. **Statistics.** Spearman ρ and Kendall τ_b, with bootstrap CIs resampled over models *and* over items. Plus **pairwise order agreement restricted to model pairs whose reference scores differ by more than their combined 95% CI** — correlating against noise otherwise inflates ρ.
6. **Acceptance targets:** held-out ρ ≥ 0.90; pairwise agreement ≥ 0.85; monotone recovery of both scaling ladders across ≥3 consecutive difficulty levels.
7. **Cost claim, quantified.** Report `n_80%` — items needed for 80% power to detect the observed gap at α=0.05 — for SciCode vs. the proxy at matched difficulty, alongside token counts, wall-clock, and per-item curation cost.

## Scope

**In scope for v0:** 4 families × 5 difficulty levels × ~30 instances (~600 items) plus Mode M variants; harness-agnostic generator + scorer; frozen JSONL snapshot; validation report.

**Out of scope for v0:** additional families, paper-derived "realism tier," multi-language support, RL/training use.

## Milestones

- [ ] Design agreed (this issue)
- [ ] Generator interface + `numcalc` end-to-end + sandboxed grader + CI gold-solution check
- [ ] Remaining three families, two-implementation gate applied, v0 snapshot frozen
- [ ] Reference SciCode measured across roster
- [ ] Proxy sweep, presets tuned on dev families only
- [ ] Held-out correlation + D50 curves + power analysis + memorization probes
- [ ] PR: generator, dataset, scorer, harness wiring, docs, validation report

## Some questions:

1. **What model scale must show signal?** Does this need to discriminate ~300M ablation checkpoints, or is 8B+ sufficient? This determines whether Mode M is essential or optional.
2. **Which harness should it land in** — evalchemy post-hoc, Harbor, or a custom evaluator under `lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/evaluators`? I plan to keep the generator and scorer harness-agnostic either way.
3. **Is a code-execution sandbox available in the eval path** as Numerical tolerances depend on versions of different libraries like numpy/scipy.
4. Is cluster time available if I want to run > 8B models?

comments.author: Nativeatom
comments.body:
The multidimensional vector evaluation looks great. 

There are results from more recent models in 
[Artificial Analysis](https://artificialanalysis.ai/evaluations/scicode) and [LLM Registry](https://llm-registry.com/benchmark/scicode?view=all&variants=0&range=all), are they in the same scale compared to the original set?

Meanwhile, what do you feel is the major challenge here, the correct programing-level understanding of scientific knowledge, or the difficulty in thoroughly implementing the snippet (e.g. coverage of boundary conditions, memorizing all the constants correctly)?

comments.author: ayush1298
comments.body:
@Nativeatom, below are answers to your questions as per my analysis: 

## 1. Same scale as the paper?

No. The paper's **4.6%** is **main-problem** accuracy — all-or-nothing over a chain, using the model's own prior steps. AA's ~60% is the **subproblem** metric over the 288 test-set subproblems. Different denominator and aggregation.

**LLM Registry isn't a second data point** as it lists AA as its source and the numbers match (Gemini 3.1 Pro 59.0% vs 58.9%). 

**The bigger issue is compression.** Median 44%, top three within 1.5 points. At n=288 the SE at p=0.6 is 2.9pp — and subproblems are nested in 80 main problems, so at ICC 0.2 effective n is ~190 and SE rises to ~3.6pp. Minimum detectable difference on unpaired aggregates is **~11pp**. The top of that leaderboard is one statistical tie.

Two consequences: run the reference ourselves for **per-item** results, since paired comparison is far more powerful than the above; and restrict the correlation target to model pairs actually separated in the reference, or ρ is attenuated and uninterpretable.

It also sharpens the motivation that SciCode has a **floor problem at small scale** *and* a **ceiling-compression problem at the frontier**, which is why the headline metric is `D50` rather than a raw pass rate.

## 2. Scientific Knowledge or snippet implementation?

**Both, binding at different scales.** Knowledge gates whether a small model attempts the right algorithm at all; implementation thoroughness is what's compressing the top.

The Ewald example on AA's own page: all four energy terms are given in full LaTeX, so barely any derivation remains. What's left is broadcasting bookkeeping (`(natoms, npairs, 1, 3)` against `(natoms, 1, ncells, 3)`), an exclusion rule stated purely as boundary conditions, and unit discipline (zJ / nm/ps / g·mol⁻¹, `kB = 0.0138064852 zJ/K`, a g/mol → kg/particle conversion). A model can know exactly what Ewald summation is and fail all of it.

On the contrary, EAIRA's SciCode analysis found significant gains from supplying scientific background, which reads as a real reasoning limit rather than a coding one.

So rather than assert a winner, the proposal now includes two mechanisms that measure the split directly, neither needing a judge model . **dual grading** (strict vs. convention-tolerant; the gap is the implementation tax) and an **automatic error taxonomy** separating "right shape, values far off" (knowledge — wrong algorithm) from "right shape, outside tolerance" (implementation — convention, units, off-by-one). That ratio gives the split per model and per difficulty level. My prediction is that it flips from knowledge- to implementation-dominated somewhere in the 3–7B range.

comments.author: penfever
comments.body: @Nativeatom please follow up whenever you get a chance?

comments.author: rfgordan
comments.body:
There are a lot of cool ideas here. 

A couple thoughts on the goals of this work, related to your last question: 

> What model scale must show signal? Does this need to discriminate ~300M ablation checkpoints, or is 8B+ sufficient? This determines whether Mode M is essential or optional.

My understanding is that the critical piece here is discriminating the post-training checkpoints (I believe I've seen RL experiments down to 1B). I think the pretraining metrics can be deferred to future work. Also, in the validation plan here its called out that the eval should be "substantially lower cost". I think cost is a nice property but it's not highlighted as a primary goal in the Epic.

With that in mind, I would consider what the minimum viable version of this that still discriminates at lower scales would be. For example, Mode G + the first three difficulty vectors are quite intuitive as easier versions of SciCode, so require a little bit less faith in the statistical machinery proposed here. Worth testing how low you can go with just those. Relatedly, with something like the D50 metric, I'd be worried that there may be some reliance on properties of the underlying scaling curve that aren't guaranteed.

issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
The marin SFT launcher (`experiments/sft/`) has two latent bugs on the **GPU (CoreWeave H100)** path that block a full-parameter SFT of any non-trivial checkpoint. Both surfaced running a 25B dense SFT (`delphi-1e23`) on a single `8xH100` node, and both are specific to the GPU path — the recipe was previously validated only on TPU, where `ResourceConfig.with_tpu` sizes the host from the slice, so neither was ever exercised. The training child dies before completing a step in both cases. Suggested fixes below (the first is already applied in a working tree and can be upstreamed as-is).

## Bug 1 — GPU pod gets no host RAM, OOMs during `initialize_from_hf`

`experiments/sft/launcher.py::resources_from_accelerator` built the GPU `ResourceConfig` with `with_gpu(variant, count=..., regions=[ANY_REGION])` and **no `ram=`/`cpu=`/`disk=`**, so it inherited the `ResourceConfig` default of ~4 GB host RAM. `initialize_from_hf` buffers the entire HF state dict in **host RAM** before device placement (Levanter `_load_from_remote`); a 25B fp32 checkpoint is ~100 GB, so the child is `SIGKILL`ed reading the first ~2.8 GB shard. The failure is silent — no traceback, just an OOMKill — and Iris surfaces the last-flushed stdout line as a misleading "reason", so it reads like a checkpoint/IO error rather than host-RAM exhaustion.

**Suggested fix (applied, working):** size host cpu/ram/disk with the GPU count in the GPU branch, mirroring what `with_tpu` already does per slice. The node (`gd-8xh100ib-i128`) is 128 vCPU / 2 TB, so per-device 8 vCPU / 96 GB / 48 GB (→ `8xH100` = 64 vCPU / 768 GB / 384 GB) is comfortable headroom:

```python
_GPU_HOST_CPU_PER_DEVICE = 8
_GPU_HOST_RAM_GB_PER_DEVICE = 96
_GPU_HOST_DISK_GB_PER_DEVICE = 48

def resources_from_accelerator(accelerator: str) -> ResourceConfig:
    gpu = _GPU_ACCELERATOR.fullmatch(accelerator)
    if gpu is not None:
        count = int(gpu["count"])
        return ResourceConfig.with_gpu(
            gpu["variant"], count=count, regions=[ANY_REGION],
            cpu=_GPU_HOST_CPU_PER_DEVICE * count,
            ram=f"{_GPU_HOST_RAM_GB_PER_DEVICE * count}g",
            disk=f"{_GPU_HOST_DISK_GB_PER_DEVICE * count}g",
        )
    return ResourceConfig.with_tpu(accelerator)
```

(Resources are a runtime arg excluded from the step fingerprint, so this does not fork any cached artifact.)

## Bug 2 — tokenizer staging rejects `s3://`/`gs://` paths (`HFValidationError`)

When a `ModelSource` resolves the tokenizer path to an object-store dir (e.g. `PreparedModel`, whose `tokenizer_path = ctx.artifact_path(step)` is `s3://…` / `gs://…`), the SFT dies **before compile** with:

```
HFValidationError: Repo id must be in the form '.../...' … 's3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/checkpoints/delphi-1e23-prepared/2026.07.19'
```

The **weights** path handles URL-like ids: `compat/hf_checkpoints.py` routes `if "://" in id` through fsspec (`_load_state_dict` ~L752) and loads the HF config under `_patch_hf_hub_download()` (~L1599), whose `custom_validate_repo_id` bypasses `validate_repo_id` for `_is_url_like` ids (~L1306). But the **tokenizer** staging path does not: `levanter/tokenizers.py::load_tokenizer` (~L732) → `_stage_tokenizer` → `_stage_from_hf` (~L857) calls `huggingface_hub.snapshot_download(name_or_path, allow_patterns=…)` (~L868) **with no `_is_url_like` guard and outside `_patch_hf_hub_download()`**, so `validate_repo_id` rejects the object-store dir.

**Suggested fix:** in `levanter/tokenizers.py`, add a `_is_url_like` check so URL-like tokenizer paths are fetched via fsspec (download the tokenizer files from the `s3://`/`gs://` dir) instead of being handed raw to `snapshot_download`/`validate_repo_id` — or, minimally, wrap the `snapshot_download` in the same `_patch_hf_hub_download()` context the weights path uses so the URL bypass applies uniformly. Either makes the tokenizer path consistent with the already-URL-aware weights path.

**Current workaround** (does not need the fix): point the SFT `ModelSource` at an HF **repo id** rather than an object-store dir (the `HFModel(model_ref=<hf repo>)` path, which the proven `delphi_1e22` config uses). That is why `PreparedModel(step=…)` — designed to init from a prep-step's object-store output — is unusable on this path today.

## Impact / scope

- Bug 1 affects **every** GPU SFT of a checkpoint whose host-RAM state dict exceeds ~4 GB (i.e. anything past a small model), independent of dataset.
- Bug 2 affects any `ModelSource` that resolves the tokenizer to an `s3://`/`gs://` dir — notably `PreparedModel`, making the reproducible "prep-step → init-from-step-output" flow unusable on GPU/CoreWeave until fixed; the HF-repo staging workaround is the only path today.

Both are in the `experiments/sft/` + Levanter tokenizer-staging code and were confirmed by an end-to-end 25B `8xH100` run that, once both were addressed, compiles and trains cleanly (first step 30.9 s, ~4.3 s/it).

issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
## What is present vs. missing (precise)

**Present — Grug MoE trains on both TPU and GPU today, but entirely through JAX (Levanter/Haliax):**
- TPU path (megablox Pallas GMM) drives the **67B-A2B run** on v4-2048 (#6044).
- GPU path is **validated end-to-end on H100**: Grug MoE ran on CoreWeave first-try (#3025), plus active MFU optimization (#4302, #6367 d2560 H100 MFU, #6493 Muon single-node GPU, #6492), enabled by the **Triton `ragged_dot`** fallback (PR #4297) and **DeepEP** dispatch (#6251); ring EP lowers + executes on GPU (#6532). Blackwell/B200 via QuACK is WIP (#7012, #6597).

**Present on the PyTorch side too:** MarinSkyRL **already trains MoE policies in PyTorch** — GRPO on Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B / Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (#7052, #6335). So "MoE in PyTorch" is *not* missing.

**Missing:** there is **no PyTorch implementation of the Grug kernels**, and no bridge that lets MarinSkyRL inherit Grug's kernel performance or verify numerical parity against it. The boundary MarinSkyRL faces is **JAX→PyTorch (framework)** — orthogonal to, and harder than, the **TPU→GPU (hardware)** boundary, which is largely solved. Direct extraction of the JAX/Pallas kernels into PyTorch is not viable (megablox is a JAX `pallas_call`/Mosaic op with no standalone form; PyTorch interop was explicitly out of scope in the kernel epic #5328). The realistic path is **share the same *upstream* kernels** (SonicMoE/QuACK, DeepEP, vLLM/SGLang fused_moe — all PyTorch-native) behind a common `grouped_gemm(lhs, rhs, group_sizes)` + dispatch/combine interface, and use the **Grug JAX forward/backward as a numerical oracle**. The gaps below are what that requires.

---

## Gaps (isolated scope · criticality · definition of done · links)

> **MarinSkyRL status (2026-08-05):** the PyTorch Grug path landed in marin-community/MarinSkyRL#110 (canonical `grug_moe` model + FSDP2 RL, reference impl checked against the committed Levanter oracle). G5 and G6 are completed; G1/G2/G3/G4 ride on the grouped-EP work in marin-community/MarinSkyRL#276 (open) plus the merged parity/divergence tests below.

### G1 — Fast grouped-GEMM expert kernel in the MarinSkyRL trainer — 🚧 in progress
**MarinSkyRL:** marin-community/MarinSkyRL#276 (open) adds native grouped MM for Grug with a 109.6× one-H100 benchmark; not yet merged.
**Scope:** Confirm what expert-GEMM the MarinSkyRL MoE training forward uses today (reference torch loop vs. a fused grouped-GEMM). If it's a reference path, back it with a PyTorch-native fast kernel (SonicMoE/QuACK CUTLASS, `grouped_gemm`, or vLLM `fused_moe`).
**Criticality: Medium** — throughput only; it *works* today, the upside is trainer step-time at 30B-A3B+. (RL is rollout-bound, so this is secondary to G3.)
**DoD:** trainer MoE layer calls a fused grouped-GEMM; measured step-time delta vs. the reference on the target 30B-A3B/35B-A3B; no regression in loss curve.
**Links:** #7012 (QuACK SM100), #5328 (SonicMoE epic — the JAX counterpart), #7052 (RL step-time feasibility).

### G2 — Backward-pass numerical parity for the fused expert GEMM — 🚧 partial
**MarinSkyRL:** marin-community/MarinSkyRL#110 (merged) keeps the reference PyTorch backward checkable against the Levanter oracle; marin-community/MarinSkyRL#276 (open) adds the four-H100 raw-gradient/AdamW parity. The custom-vs-recompute decision and finite-difference gate ride on #276.
**Scope:** Any fused grouped-GEMM needs a hand-written PyTorch backward (`autograd.Function`). Verify it against a reference. Marin's JAX experience is the warning: every custom path needed a `custom_vjp`, and #5328's `unpack_bwd` study found the fancy Pallas backward bought ~2.8% e2e vs. +21.8% for plain forced-recompute — i.e. the custom backward frequently isn't worth it.
**Criticality: Critical** — a wrong backward silently biases gradients with no crash.
**DoD:** PyTorch backward matches finite-difference AND matches the Grug JAX gradient (via G5) within tolerance on a fixed (tokens, router-logits, weights) case; decision recorded on whether a custom backward beats plain recompute.
**Links:** #5328 (unpack_bwd decision log), PR #4297 (Triton custom_vjp).

### G3 — Train↔rollout routing-semantics parity — 🚧 partial
**MarinSkyRL:** marin-community/MarinSkyRL#110 (merged) synchronizes mixed BF16/FP32 routing state to vLLM; marin-community/MarinSkyRL#280 (merged) adds a policy-forward capture/replay harness that re-runs the trainer boundary without rollout/inference. The explicit trainer↔inference expert-assignment + gate-weight parity test rides on marin-community/MarinSkyRL#276 (open).
**Scope:** top-k selection, token-sort order, and tie-breaking must be identical between the MarinSkyRL trainer forward and the rollout/inference engine (vLLM/SGLang) forward. Any divergence injects policy-gradient bias.
**Criticality: Critical** — this is the RL-specific trap: MarinSkyRL already runs TIS/R3 to correct train↔infer mismatch (#6335), and a routing mismatch compounds exactly what TIS is meant to fix. #6044 flagged the local token-sort for QB routing as hardware-dependent.
**DoD:** a parity test asserting identical expert assignments + gate weights between trainer and inference engine on a fixed batch; the tie-break rule is documented and enforced in both.
**Links:** #6335 (TIS/R3 on MarinSkyRL), #6044 (token-sort hw-dependence), #7052.

### G4 — EP dispatch/combine reduction parity (only if EP>1 in the trainer) — 🚧 in progress
**MarinSkyRL:** marin-community/MarinSkyRL#276 (open) delivers torch all-to-all EP with averaged expert gradients + the mixed-EP lifecycle capstone (global expert-row gather, checkpoint continuation, multi-owner FP32 bias readback). Collective divergence is bounded by the merged marin-community/MarinSkyRL#288, #272, #271, #270, #269, #268 (EP4/FSDP4 mesh schedules).
**Scope:** If MarinSkyRL trains at expert-parallel degree >1, the dispatch/combine (DeepEP, which both stacks can share upstream; or all_gather+reduce_scatter) must be reduction-order-consistent with what produced the reference gradients.
**Criticality: Medium** — bites only at EP>1; the current 30B-A3B RL may run EP=1. Downgrade to Low if EP=1 is confirmed.
**DoD:** EP combine is reduction-consistent and validated at the EP degree MarinSkyRL actually uses; DeepEP wired as the shared transport if EP>1.
**Links:** PR #6251 (assigned-token DeepEP dispatch, closed) + the landed `_moe/ep_deepep.py` backend, #6532 (ring-EP-on-GPU + megablox `shard_map` lowering findings).

### G5 — Cross-framework parity harness (Grug JAX forward/backward as oracle) — ✅ completed
**MarinSkyRL:** marin-community/MarinSkyRL#110 (merged) keeps the reference PyTorch `grug_moe` forward/backward/routing/bias checkable against the committed Levanter oracle without adding JAX to the runtime; validation report linked in the PR. This is the runnable oracle harness the DoD asks for.
**Scope:** Build a harness that runs a fixed input (tokens + router logits + expert weights) through both the Grug JAX MoE layer and the MarinSkyRL PyTorch MoE layer, and diffs routing decisions, per-expert outputs, and gradients.
**Criticality: High** — it's the enabling infrastructure for G2/G3/G4; without it, "parity" is unfalsifiable.
**DoD:** a runnable harness + a committed tolerance report for the target model; wired into CI or a manual gate before MoE-kernel changes land in MarinSkyRL.
**Links:** #2828 (established the shared `(lhs, rhs, group_sizes)` API), #5328.

### G6 — MoE checkpoint / expert-weight-layout interop (only if weights cross frameworks) — ✅ completed (N/A)
**MarinSkyRL:** the gap is moot by the issue's own escape clause ("N/A if MarinSkyRL loads HF-format weights directly"): marin-community/MarinSkyRL#110 (merged) loads HF safetensors straight into the PyTorch `grug_moe` and synchronizes mixed BF16/FP32 state to vLLM, so no Levanter↔PyTorch expert-tensor converter is needed. EP-owner transfer readback is covered by marin-community/MarinSkyRL#276 (open).
**Scope:** If Grug-trained (Levanter/JAX) MoE checkpoints feed the PyTorch RL policy — or MOPD/distillation moves experts between them — the expert weight layout (gate/up/down packing, expert-major vs. token-major, sharded vs. dense) must be mapped and tested.
**Criticality: Medium** — only if checkpoints actually cross the JAX↔PyTorch boundary; N/A if MarinSkyRL loads HF-format weights directly.
**DoD:** a documented, round-trip-tested weight converter for MoE expert tensors between Levanter and the PyTorch model; parity of a forward pass on converted weights.
**Links:** — (new); relate to the hero-model MOPD path if/when specced.

---

## Suggested sequencing
G5 (oracle harness) first — it unblocks the two Critical correctness gaps. Then G3 (routing parity, the RL-specific trap) and G2 (backward parity) in parallel. G1 (perf) and G4/G6 (conditional) follow once correctness is proven. Confirm the open scoping questions early: (a) what expert-GEMM MarinSkyRL uses today, (b) its EP degree, (c) whether checkpoints cross the JAX↔PyTorch boundary — these set the criticality of G1/G4/G6.

## References
Runs/experiments: #6044 (67B-A2B TPU), #3025 (Grug MoE on CW GPU, first-try), #4302 / #6367 / #6493 / #6492 (H100 MFU), #7012 (B200 QuACK), #6597 (fused EP NVLink), #7052 (MarinSkyRL 30B/35B-A3B RL step-time), #6335 (TIS/R3 on MarinSkyRL).
Kernels/PRs: #2828 (GPU port + shared API), PR #4297 (Triton ragged_dot, merged), PR #5718 (sonic gather/combine, merged), PR #6251 (assigned-token DeepEP dispatch, closed), #5328 (SonicMoE epic), #6532 (zero-bubble PP for Grug-MoE — ring-EP-GPU + megablox `shard_map` findings), #3431 (abandoned fused TPU-EP).
Code: `lib/haliax/src/haliax/nn/ragged_dot.py:18-23,335-360`; `lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/grug_moe.py:184-217`; `lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/{local.py:32,scatter.py,sonic.py,ep_ring.py,ep_deepep.py}`; `experiments/june_tpu_67b_a2b/moe/model.py:121,512`.

comments.author: penfever
comments.body:
🤖 **Fast-track addendum: the checkpoint→GPU path already exists (HF-native); the residual is *one* training modeling class.**

Digging into the recent GPU-serving work (#6869, PR #6966, PR #6891, marin-community/vllm#7) sharpens **G6** and collapses the "get RL running on Grug MoEs" critical path. What's already built, then the one concrete TODO.

## Already built (checkpoint interop is ~solved for *serving*)

1. **Export is HF-native.** `experiments/grug/moe/model.py` defines `GrugMoeHfConfig(HfConfig)` (L96) + architecture `"GrugMoeForCausalLM"` (L56); the Levanter checkpoint exports through the standard `HFCheckpointConverter` (`to_hf_config()`) → a plain HF checkpoint (`config.json` + safetensors).
2. **GPU rollout serving is done.** `marin-community/vllm` ships a native PyTorch `grugmoe.py` (`GrugMoeRouter` / `GrugMoeGatedNorm` / `GrugMoeMLP`) that `load_weights` the HF checkpoint and runs experts on vLLM **`FusedMoE`** + expert parallelism — preserving Levanter's router math incl. the `1e-9` combine-weight epsilon (marin-community/vllm#7). Parity-validated vs a JAX bf16 reference (PR #6966/#6891) on `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/grug/moe_may_compute_opt_d512_ep1-05c39b/checkpoints/step-10980` (DP8/EP8 on one H100×8, TP=1); the 67B BF16 export was exercised DP8/EP8.

Note: GPU serving uses **vLLM FusedMoE, not the Grug JAX kernels** — the "share upstream kernels" pattern; the Grug JAX kernels never cross into the GPU rollout path.

## Fast-track TODO — the one thing actually missing

**→ Write a *training* `GrugMoeForCausalLM` PyTorch modeling class.** The config, the arch string, and an *inference* model (the vLLM fork) all exist; what's missing is a training-capable forward+backward. Concretely:
- reuse `GrugMoeHfConfig` and lift `GrugMoeRouter` (top-k + the `1e-9` epsilon) **verbatim** from the vLLM fork — that's what buys train↔rollout parity;
- replace vLLM's inference `FusedMoE` with a **training-capable expert forward**: start with a reference grouped-GEMM (dense/loop over experts) → autograd-correct, *no* custom backward; drop in SonicMoE/QuACK/`grouped_gemm` + a hand-written backward later (that's G1/G2, deferred);
- load the exported safetensors via the same weight-key mapping vLLM's `load_weights` uses.

**→ Load it into MarinSkyRL via `from_pretrained`** — the exact path #7052 used for Qwen-Coder-30B-A3B. Start on the parity-validated `moe_may_compute_opt_d512_ep1` step-10980 checkpoint, EP=1/8, **TIS on** (#6335) to absorb the expert-GEMM numeric residual.

Everything else in this issue (**G1** fast kernel, **G2** custom backward, **G3** routing parity, **G4** EP, **G5** parity harness) becomes the **parallel track** — gated behind TIS + the RL-parity checklist #6341, not blockers. The fast-track is ~one modeling file, not a kernel project.

## "How do you add a custom model to HF short of a PR?"

You don't need a `transformers` PR. Three options, easiest first:
- **(a) In-repo class in MarinSkyRL** — define `GrugMoeForCausalLM(PreTrainedModel)` in the RL repo, construct the policy from it directly, `load_state_dict` the safetensors. No HF Hub, no `Auto*` registration, no `trust_remote_code`. Simplest when the trainer is the only consumer.
- **(b) `trust_remote_code` custom-code-on-Hub — ✅ PREFERRED** — ship `configuration_grugmoe.py` + `modeling_grugmoe.py` next to the checkpoint (HF repo or local dir) with an `auto_map` in `config.json`; `from_pretrained(..., trust_remote_code=True)` loads it anywhere (the MarinSkyRL trainer *and* any other consumer — eval, a second RL stack, a notebook) with one call, no per-repo model code and no upstream `transformers` PR. This is the right default: the *training* class lives with the checkpoint and is reused by everyone. *Caveat:* the HF mirror must include the `.py` files (our `mirror_hf_to_gcs.py` `INCLUDE_PATTERNS` needs `.py` for `auto_map` models, or they silently don't ride along).
- **(c) Upstream to `transformers`** — a real PR; only worth it for broad external reuse, not needed here.

The vLLM side effectively took a 4th route (a vendored model in a vLLM *fork*). **Go with (b)** — publish `modeling_grugmoe.py` + `auto_map` alongside the checkpoint so the training class is Hub-portable and any consumer loads it via `from_pretrained(trust_remote_code=True)`; keep (a) only as a throwaway in-repo stopgap if you need something running before the Hub files land.

**Bottom line:** because the export is already HF-format and the vLLM fork already proves the PyTorch router/attention/weight-mapping, "RL on Grug MoEs" fast-tracks to **write one training `GrugMoeForCausalLM` + `from_pretrained` it into MarinSkyRL** — with parity as the parallel track.

issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
## TL;DR We ran Marin's Stage 0 protocol gate on four untrained MoE base checkpoints, serving each with its own shipped chat template and with the shared Stage 0 SFT template. All four already write assistant-style answers to chat prompts. Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-Base ends 100% of chat turns with `<|im_end|>` and, under the shared template, which does not prompt for thinking, opens a `` block on 194 of 200 math prompts. Snowball's base (`open-athena/snowball-67b-a2b-base-262k-qk175`) ends 97.5–99% of chat turns with the Llama 3 turn token `<|eot_id|>`. Qwen3-30B-A3B-Base ends its answers with `<|endoftext|>` and never thinks. Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-Base never stops on its own. So these "base" checkpoints start Stage 0 with very different learned chat and reasoning behavior. This issue has everything needed to rerun the measurement. ## Description Marin's on-policy distillation (OPD) interference experiment starts from one checkpoint per MoE architecture. Stage 0 is a three-stage SFT run (chat, then thinking, then terminal-agent data) that turns each base into a checkpoint called `B`. `B` must pass a gate before later stages use it. The protocol part of the gate requires at least 98% of replies to end with the end-of-turn token, and at least 98% of think blocks to close. Qwen3-MoE's `B` failed it: it closed its think block on only 27–63% of replies and ended only 90% of P_think turns. This raised a question: is the failure caused by SFT, or by what each base already knew before SFT? This experiment runs the same gate on the bases. The gate (`protocol_gate.py`, below) serves a checkpoint with vLLM on one 8×H100 node: data parallel 8 with expert parallelism, no reasoning parser, and special tokens kept in the output. It samples one completion per prompt at temperature 0.6 and top_p 0.95, at repetition penalties 1.0 and 1.05. - **Turn ended:** vLLM stopped on the family's end-of-turn token, `<|im_end|>` for Qwen and Nemotron and `<|eot_id|>` for Snowball. The gate uses the same token for both templates. Generation ignores EOS and stops only on that token, so a reply that ends with the base's EOS runs to the token cap and counts as not ended. - **Think closed:** every think-open marker in the reply has a matching close marker. The prompts are 200 UltraChat conversations (P_chat, up to 13 messages, ending on a user turn) and 200 OlympiadBench problems (P_think, one user turn). They're in [this gist](https://gist.github.com/penfever/c97633c564789116f7a01b567575ba2a) as `gate_chat.jsonl` and `gate_think.jsonl`. Each row has `probe_id`, `source`, `answer`, `metadata` and an OpenAI-style `messages` list; the gate reads only `probe_id` and `messages`. The two templates: - **Native:** the `chat_template` the base ships in `tokenizer_config.json`. Nemotron ships none, so it has no native run. - **Shared:** the Stage 0 SFT template from `chat_template.py` (below). It is one Jinja skeleton with per-family delimiters. The family keys are `qwen3_moe`, `qwen3_5_moe`, `nemotron_h` and `grug`; Grug is the Marin MoE architecture behind Snowball. - Qwen: `<|im_start|>`/`<|im_end|>` turns with ``/``, no newlines around the tags. - Nemotron: the same delimiters as Qwen, plus a BOS token. - Snowball: Llama 3 `<|start_header_id|>`…`<|end_header_id|>` turns ended by `<|eot_id|>`, with `<|start_think|>`/`<|end_think|>` in Llama 3's reserved token slots 128002 and 128003. Compared with Qwen's own template, it has no reasoning-history truncation and no injected empty think block. Tool results get their own `tool` role. ## Results Repetition penalty 1.05, 200 prompts per set. The repetition penalty 1.0 reports are written next to these. All runs served Hugging Face `main` for the weights. On 2026-10-28, `main` of each repo was the revision in the table, and none of the four repos had changed since before the runs. The shared-template tokenizer files were pinned to that revision explicitly. | Base (HF revision) | Template | P_chat turn ended | P_think turn ended | Replies opening a think block (P_chat / P_think) | Think closed | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Base` (`1b75feb7`) | native | 0% | 0% | 0 / 0 | n/a | | same | shared | 0%* | 0%* | 0 / 0 | n/a | | `Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-Base` (`0f081307`) | native | 100% | 57.5%* | all, via the template's prefilled `\n`† | 100% / 59.5%† | | same | shared | 100% | 61.5%* | 58 / 194 | 100% / 62% | | `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-Base-BF16` (`e0ac9ee3`) | shared | 0% | 0% | 1 / 12 | 1 of 1 / 1 of 12 | | `open-athena/snowball-67b-a2b-base-262k-qk175` (`11c9430d`) | native | 99% | 58.5%* | 0 / 0 | n/a | | same | shared | 97.5% | 64.5%* | 0 / 0 | n/a | | Qwen3-MoE `B` (Stage 0 output), for reference | shared | 98.5% | 90% | 197 / 200 | 27% / 63% | | Snowball `B` (Stage 0 output), for reference | shared | 99.0% | 98.5% | 157 / 200 | 99.4% / 98.5% | \* These runs used an 8,192-token cap. The first attempts at the full caps (24,576 for Qwen3, whose context is 32,768, and the gate's default 32,768 otherwise) failed with HTTP 504 from the inference proxy on long requests. Qwen3 native and Nemotron completed at the full cap; we did not diagnose why the others timed out. P_think turn ends are therefore understated by truncated long solutions. In the capped runs whose chat turns end (Qwen3.5 and Snowball), P_chat replies average 1.7k–5.3k characters and are unaffected. † Qwen3.5's native template ends the generation prompt with `\n` unless `enable_thinking=False`. The reply starts inside a think block, so the gate counts no opening marker. The closure share here is the share of replies containing ``, counted from the raw completions. What the raw completions show: - **Qwen3 base:** finished assistant answers ("Certainly! Our range of postal tubes includes…") and clean step-by-step math. 97% of P_chat and 98.5% of P_think replies contain `<|endoftext|>`, its pretraining EOS, and then run on to the token cap. It never writes `<|im_end|>` or ``. - **Nemotron base:** assistant-style answers ("Sure! … Is there anything else I can help you with?") that run on into a made-up next exchange. It never emits `<|im_end|>`, and all 400 replies run to the token cap. - **Snowball base:** a complete answer followed by `<|eot_id|>` under either template. It never emits `<|start_think|>`. In 10–12% of P_think replies it writes a plain-text ``, and a plain-text `` in only 0.5–2.5%. That pattern matches reasoning traces in the DeepSeek-R1 layout, where `` sits on the prompt side. - **Qwen3.5 base:** under its native template, the prefilled think block holds Qwen-style reasoning ("Okay, the user is asking for more details about…") and closes with `` before the answer. Under the shared template, whose training layout puts no newline after `` and whose generation prompt does not prefill one, it opens with `\n`, which is Qwen's native newline layout. ## Conclusions - None of the four checkpoints behaves like a raw pretrained model on chat prompts. They differ in which chat protocol they have learned: - Qwen3.5 has ChatML turns and Qwen-style thinking. - Snowball has Llama 3 turns but no thinking. - Qwen3 has assistant answers but ends them with its document EOS. - Nemotron has assistant answers with no stopping behavior. - These checkpoints start Stage 0 with very different learned chat and reasoning behavior. Experiments that compare SFT effects across them should account for that. - For Snowball, the shared template's turn structure matches the base's behavior: 97.5% of chat turns end under the shared template and 99% under the native one. The `<|start_think|>`/`<|end_think|>` markers are new to the base and are taught from scratch. The plain-text `` habit is the one competing pattern we observed. Snowball's `B` passed think closure at ≥98% on this template. - Qwen3's base never opens a think block. Its `B` learned to open one and often fails to close it. We have not tested whether the shared template's no-newline `` layout, which differs from Qwen's native `\n…\n\n\n`, causes this. - This measures behavior, not provenance. It doesn't show which data or training stage taught each protocol. For Snowball, the data mix of the pre-training, cooldown and `262k-qk175` long-context stages would answer that. Related: #10695 (Snowball identity) and #10400 (extra think segments in Grug checkpoints). ## Reproduce You need Iris submit access to CoreWeave `cw-rno2a`, CoreWeave S3 credentials for your upload, a Hugging Face token, the GitHub CLI, and H100 capacity. Each run is a small CPU job that starts its own 8×H100 vLLM job, for about 3–5 H100-hours. 1. Check out main at `2cae063c87`. The runs used a branch based on it, with the serving and evaluation code unchanged. Add the two gate files below at `experiments/post_training/chat_template.py` and `experiments/post_training/stage0/protocol_gate.py`. 2. Put `submit_base_gate.sh`, `base_gate.py` and `inspect_completions.py` in one directory, `D`. 3. Pick a CoreWeave S3 prefix that both you and `cw-rno2a` jobs can read and write, for example under `s3://marin-rno2a/marin/users//`, and export it as `G`. Download the prompts and upload them under their own names: `gh gist clone c97633c564789116f7a01b567575ba2a gate-prompts && uv run fsutil cp gate-prompts/gate_chat.jsonl gate-prompts/gate_think.jsonl $G/`. 4. From the checkout root, with `HF_TOKEN` and `G` exported, submit each run. ```bash D=path/to/scripts bash $D/submit_base_gate.sh qwen3_moe native qwen3r --max-model-len 32768 --max-tokens 24576 bash $D/submit_base_gate.sh qwen3_moe shared qwen3s8k --max-model-len 32768 --max-tokens 8192 bash $D/submit_base_gate.sh qwen3_5_moe native qwen35n8k --max-tokens 8192 bash $D/submit_base_gate.sh qwen3_5_moe shared qwen35s8k --max-tokens 8192 bash $D/submit_base_gate.sh nemotron_h shared nemotronh2 bash $D/submit_base_gate.sh grug native snowballn8k --max-tokens 8192 bash $D/submit_base_gate.sh grug shared snowballs8k --max-tokens 8192 ``` Under zsh, keep this in a bash script or `bash -c`, because zsh does not split unquoted variables into separate arguments. base_gate.py ```python """Scratch: Stage 0 protocol gate on an untrained base, with its native or the shared template.""" import dataclasses, json, pathlib, sys, tempfile import fsspec from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download import experiments.post_training.stage0.protocol_gate as gate from experiments.post_training.chat_template import FAMILY_TOKEN_MAPS, FAMILY_TOKENIZER_REVISIONS, shared_template family, template_kind, tokenizer_uri = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3] repo, revision = FAMILY_TOKENIZER_REVISIONS[family] if template_kind == "shared": local = pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) snapshot_download(repo, revision=revision, local_dir=local, allow_patterns=["*.json", "*.txt", "*.jinja", "*.model", "*.tiktoken"], ignore_patterns=["*.safetensors.index.json"]) template = shared_template(FAMILY_TOKEN_MAPS[family]) config = json.loads((local / "tokenizer_config.json").read_text()) config["chat_template"] = template (local / "tokenizer_config.json").write_text(json.dumps(config, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)) (local / "chat_template.jinja").write_text(template) # NemotronH's config points auto_map at remote code this folder does not carry; transformers 5 has the class. model_config = json.loads((local / "config.json").read_text()) model_config.pop("auto_map", None) (local / "config.json").write_text(json.dumps(model_config, indent=2)) for path in local.iterdir(): if path.is_file(): with open(path, "rb") as src, fsspec.open(f"{tokenizer_uri}/{path.name}", "wb") as dst: dst.write(src.read()) print("uploaded shared-template tokenizer", tokenizer_uri, sorted(p.name for p in local.iterdir()), flush=True) original = gate.checkpoint_model gate.checkpoint_model = lambda name, checkpoint, max_model_len: dataclasses.replace( original(name, checkpoint, max_model_len), tokenizer=tokenizer_uri ) sys.argv = ["protocol_gate", "--checkpoint", repo] + sys.argv[4:] gate.main() ```

experiments/post_training/stage0/protocol_gate.py ```python # Copyright The Marin Authors # SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0 """The Stage 0 gate's protocol check on a Snowball ``B``: turn ends and thinking closure. DESIGN, "Stage 0 gate": on 200 prompts per probe family, at least 98% of turns end with the end-of-turn token and at least 98% of thinking blocks close. This module serves the checkpoint with vLLM (no reasoning parser, special tokens kept), samples one completion per prompt and scores the raw text. Generation ignores the tokenizer's EOS list and stops only on the end-of-turn token, so a turn counts as ended exactly when vLLM reports that token as its stop reason; a completion that emits ``<|end_of_text|>`` instead runs on and fails. Tool-call parsing is measured on the P_agent trajectories, where the tool calls are. Run as a small CPU job; serving dispatches its own 8-GPU job:: python -m experiments.post_training.stage0.protocol_gate --checkpoint s3://.../hf/step-N \\ --prompts P_chat=s3://.../P_chat.jsonl --prompts P_think=s3://.../P_think.jsonl \\ --out s3://.../protocol.json """ from __future__ import annotations import argparse import functools import json import logging import random from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor from dataclasses import dataclass import fsspec import requests from iris.rpc import job_pb2 from marin.evaluation.eval_env import EVAL_RUNTIME_ENV_KEYS, env_vars_from_keys from marin.evaluation.hardware import AcceleratorChoice, Platform from marin.evaluation.model_config import ModelConfig, ResourceHint, ServeConfig from marin.evaluation.serving_config import inference_config_for_model from marin.inference.iris import remote_inference from marin.inference.types import OpenAIEndpoint from transformers import AutoTokenizer from experiments.evaluation.models import SNOWBALL_VLLM_ARGS from experiments.post_training.chat_template import ( FAMILY_TOKEN_MAPS, FAMILY_TOKENIZER_REVISIONS, GRUG_TOKENS, ChatTokens, ) logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) @dataclass(frozen=True) class Delimiters: """One family's think markers and the id of its end-of-turn token.""" tokens: ChatTokens end_of_turn_id: int # Grug's <|eot_id|> in the Llama 3 vocabulary. END_OF_TURN_ID = 128009 GRUG_DELIMITERS = Delimiters(GRUG_TOKENS, END_OF_TURN_ID) def family_delimiters(family: str) -> Delimiters: """A family's delimiters, with the end-of-turn id read from its pinned tokenizer.""" tokens = FAMILY_TOKEN_MAPS[family] repo, revision = FAMILY_TOKENIZER_REVISIONS[family] (end_of_turn_id,) = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(repo, revision=revision).encode( tokens.turn_close, add_special_tokens=False ) return Delimiters(tokens, end_of_turn_id) PROMPTS_PER_FAMILY = 200 MIN_TURN_END_SHARE = 0.98 MIN_THINK_CLOSE_SHARE = 0.98 MAX_COMPLETION_TOKENS = 32768 MAX_MODEL_LEN = 65536 @dataclass(frozen=True) class Decode: """The sampling settings of one gate run; the chosen one becomes B's probe decode.""" temperature: float = 0.6 top_p: float = 0.95 repetition_penalty: float = 1.0 max_tokens: int = MAX_COMPLETION_TOKENS CONCURRENT_REQUESTS = 64 REQUEST_TIMEOUT = 3600 @dataclass(frozen=True) class Completion: family: str probe_id: str finish_reason: str stop_reason: int | str | None text: str def completion_protocol( text: str, finish_reason: str, stop_reason: int | str | None, delimiters: Delimiters = GRUG_DELIMITERS ) -> dict[str, bool | int]: """One completion's protocol facts: did the turn end, and did every think block close.""" think_open, think_close = delimiters.tokens.think_open, delimiters.tokens.think_close opens = text.count(think_open) closes = text.count(think_close) return { "turn_ended": finish_reason == "stop" and stop_reason == delimiters.end_of_turn_id, "think_blocks": opens, "think_closed": opens > 0 and opens == closes and text.rfind(think_close) > text.rfind(think_open), } # Terminus-2's JSON turn carries these keys; a single-turn reply in that shape is the agent format. AGENT_TURN_KEYS = ('"analysis"', '"plan"', '"commands"') def is_agent_turn(text: str, delimiters: Delimiters = GRUG_DELIMITERS) -> bool: """Whether a reply's answer (after any thinking) is a Terminus-2 JSON agent turn.""" answer = text.rsplit(delimiters.tokens.think_close, 1)[-1] return answer.lstrip().startswith("{") and all(key in answer for key in AGENT_TURN_KEYS) def protocol_report(completions: list[Completion], delimiters: Delimiters = GRUG_DELIMITERS) -> dict: """Per-family shares and the gate verdict.""" families: dict[str, dict] = {} for family in sorted({completion.family for completion in completions}): facts = [ completion_protocol(c.text, c.finish_reason, c.stop_reason, delimiters) for c in completions if c.family == family ] with_think = [fact for fact in facts if fact["think_blocks"]] turn_share = sum(bool(fact["turn_ended"]) for fact in facts) / len(facts) think_share = sum(bool(fact["think_closed"]) for fact in with_think) / len(with_think) if with_think else None texts = [c.text for c in completions if c.family == family] families[family] = { "completions": len(facts), # Reported, not gated (DESIGN decision log, 2026-10-24). "agent_format_share": sum(is_agent_turn(text, delimiters) for text in texts) / len(texts), "turn_end_share": turn_share, "completions_with_thinking": len(with_think), "think_close_share": think_share, "passed": turn_share >= MIN_TURN_END_SHARE and (think_share is None or think_share >= MIN_THINK_CLOSE_SHARE), } return { "passed": all(entry["passed"] for entry in families.values()), "thresholds": {"turn_end": MIN_TURN_END_SHARE, "think_close": MIN_THINK_CLOSE_SHARE}, "families": families, } def _read_prompts(path: str, count: int, seed: int) -> list[dict]: with fsspec.open(path, "rt") as handle: rows = [json.loads(line) for line in handle] return random.Random(seed).sample(rows, min(count, len(rows))) def _complete( endpoint: OpenAIEndpoint, family: str, row: dict, seed: int, decode: Decode, end_of_turn_id: int ) -> Completion: headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {endpoint.api_key}"} if endpoint.api_key else {} body = { "model": endpoint.model, "messages": row["messages"], "temperature": decode.temperature, "top_p": decode.top_p, "repetition_penalty": decode.repetition_penalty, "max_tokens": decode.max_tokens, "seed": seed, # Keep the think tokens in the text: they are what the gate counts. "skip_special_tokens": False, "ignore_eos": True, "stop_token_ids": [end_of_turn_id], } response = requests.post(endpoint.url("chat/completions"), json=body, headers=headers, timeout=REQUEST_TIMEOUT) response.raise_for_status() choice = response.json()["choices"][0] return Completion( family, row["probe_id"], choice["finish_reason"], choice.get("stop_reason"), choice["message"]["content"] or "" ) def _complete_item( endpoint: OpenAIEndpoint, seed: int, decode: Decode, end_of_turn_id: int, item: tuple[str, dict] ) -> Completion: return _complete(endpoint, item[0], item[1], seed, decode, end_of_turn_id) def checkpoint_model(name: str, checkpoint: str, max_model_len: int = MAX_MODEL_LEN) -> ModelConfig: """Serve an exported Stage 0 MoE checkpoint with its embedded template and no reasoning parser. Data parallel with expert parallelism over one 8-GPU node serves Snowball and the 30B-class Axolotl bases alike. """ return ModelConfig( name=name, location=checkpoint, tokenizer=checkpoint, apply_chat_template=True, resource_hint=ResourceHint(gpu={"H100": 8}, memory="512g", disk="500g"), serve=ServeConfig( tensor_parallel_size=1, data_parallel_size=8, max_model_len=max_model_len, max_num_batched_tokens=7168, max_num_seqs=32, auto_overrides=False, vllm_extra_args=SNOWBALL_VLLM_ARGS, ), ) def main() -> None: logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO) parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__) parser.add_argument("--checkpoint", required=True) parser.add_argument("--name", required=True, help="slash-free serving name") parser.add_argument("--prompts", action="append", required=True, help="FAMILY=path to a probe JSONL") parser.add_argument("--out", required=True) parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=0) parser.add_argument("--family", choices=sorted(FAMILY_TOKEN_MAPS), default="grug") parser.add_argument("--prompts-per-family", type=int, default=PROMPTS_PER_FAMILY) parser.add_argument( "--max-model-len", type=int, default=MAX_MODEL_LEN, help="the served context; models with a shorter native context (Qwen3-30B: 32,768) need less", ) parser.add_argument("--max-tokens", type=int, default=Decode.max_tokens, help="must leave room for the prompt") parser.add_argument("--temperature", type=float, default=Decode.temperature) parser.add_argument("--top-p", type=float, default=Decode.top_p) parser.add_argument( "--repetition-penalty", type=float, action="append", help="repeatable: each value is scored in the same serving session, into --out with a -rpX suffix", ) args = parser.parse_args() decodes = [ Decode(temperature=args.temperature, top_p=args.top_p, repetition_penalty=penalty, max_tokens=args.max_tokens) for penalty in args.repetition_penalty or [Decode.repetition_penalty] ] delimiters = GRUG_DELIMITERS if args.family == "grug" else family_delimiters(args.family) work = [ (family, row) for family, path in (spec.split("=", 1) for spec in args.prompts) for row in _read_prompts(path, args.prompts_per_family, args.seed) ] accelerator = AcceleratorChoice(platform=Platform.GPU, gpu_type="H100", gpu_count=8, target_cluster="cw-rno2a") inference = inference_config_for_model( checkpoint_model(args.name, args.checkpoint, args.max_model_len), accelerator, env_vars=env_vars_from_keys(EVAL_RUNTIME_ENV_KEYS), priority=job_pb2.PRIORITY_BAND_INHERIT, ) with remote_inference(inference) as session: endpoint = session.model.endpoint for decode in decodes: with ThreadPoolExecutor(CONCURRENT_REQUESTS) as pool: completions = list( pool.map( functools.partial(_complete_item, endpoint, args.seed, decode, delimiters.end_of_turn_id), work ) ) out = ( args.out if len(decodes) == 1 else args.out.removesuffix(".json") + f"-rp{decode.repetition_penalty:g}.json" ) _write_report(args.checkpoint, decode, completions, out, delimiters) def _write_report( checkpoint: str, decode: Decode, completions: list[Completion], out: str, delimiters: Delimiters ) -> None: report = {"checkpoint": checkpoint, "decode": decode.__dict__} report |= protocol_report(completions, delimiters) with fsspec.open(out, "w") as handle: json.dump(report, handle, indent=2) with fsspec.open(out.removesuffix(".json") + "-completions.jsonl", "w") as handle: for completion in completions: handle.write(json.dumps(completion.__dict__) + "\n") logger.info("protocol gate %s at %s: %s", "PASSED" if report["passed"] else "FAILED", decode, report["families"]) if __name__ == "__main__": main() experiments/post_training/chat_template.py ```python # Copyright The Marin Authors # SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0 """The shared chat-template structure and per-family token maps. One Jinja template renders every architecture's conversations; a family supplies only its delimiters. The template is built by baking a :class:`ChatTokens` map's strings into the skeleton as Jinja string literals, so the result is self-contained and can be frozen into a tokenizer config without importing this module at serve time. The contract the template owns: - Reasoning renders from ``reasoning_content`` on every assistant turn. There is no last-query gate, no history truncation, and no injected empty think block. - Tool calls render as ``\\n{"name": ..., "arguments": ...}\\n`` with identical JSON serialization on every family. - Tool results use bare ```` without a ``name=`` attribute, so the marker stays one token wherever the vocabulary has one. - A system turn renders only when a system message is present; none is injected. - Each assistant turn after its header, through its end-of-turn token, sits in a ``{% generation %}`` block: the completions-only training mask (Levanter and ``return_assistant_tokens_mask``). The block renders no text. Every structural delimiter in a token map must encode to exactly one token of its pinned tokenizer (:func:`validate_token_map`), so masking, stop conditions and the protocol gate are all token-exact. """ from __future__ import annotations import hashlib from dataclasses import dataclass # Placeholders baked out by shared_template(); double underscores cannot collide # with Jinja syntax or tokenizer vocabulary. _TURN_OPEN_PREFIX = "__TURN_OPEN_PREFIX__" _TURN_OPEN_SUFFIX = "__TURN_OPEN_SUFFIX__" _TURN_CLOSE = "__TURN_CLOSE__" _THINK_OPEN = "__THINK_OPEN__" _THINK_CLOSE = "__THINK_CLOSE__" _BOS = "__BOS__" _TEMPLATE_SKELETON = """{%- if '__BOS__' -%}{{ '__BOS__' }}{%- endif -%}{%- for message in messages -%} {%- if message.role == 'assistant' -%} {{- '__TURN_OPEN_PREFIX__assistant__TURN_OPEN_SUFFIX__\n' -}} {%- generation -%} {%- if message.reasoning_content -%} {{- '__THINK_OPEN__' ~ message.reasoning_content ~ '__THINK_CLOSE__' -}} {%- endif -%} {{- message.content if message.content else '' -}} {%- for call in message.tool_calls or [] -%} {%- set function = call.function if call.function is defined else call -%} {{- '\\n{"name": ' -}} {{- function.name | tojson -}} {{- ', "arguments": ' -}} {{- function.arguments if function.arguments is string else function.arguments | tojson -}} {{- '}\\n' -}} {%- endfor -%} {{- '__TURN_CLOSE__' -}} {%- endgeneration -%} {%- elif message.role == 'tool' -%} {{- '__TURN_OPEN_PREFIX__tool__TURN_OPEN_SUFFIX__\n\\n' -}} {{- message.content if message.content else '' -}} {{- '\\n__TURN_CLOSE__' -}} {%- else -%} {{- '__TURN_OPEN_PREFIX__' ~ message.role ~ '__TURN_OPEN_SUFFIX__\\n' -}} {{- message.content if message.content else '' -}} {{- '__TURN_CLOSE__' -}} {%- endif -%} {{- '\\n' -}} {%- endfor -%} {%- if add_generation_prompt -%} {{- '__TURN_OPEN_PREFIX__assistant__TURN_OPEN_SUFFIX__\n' -}} {%- endif -%}""" @dataclass(frozen=True) class ChatTokens: """One family's delimiters. ``bos`` may be empty where the family has none.""" bos: str turn_open_prefix: str turn_open_suffix: str turn_close: str think_open: str think_close: str GRUG_TOKENS = ChatTokens( bos="<|begin_of_text|>", turn_open_prefix="<|start_header_id|>", turn_open_suffix="<|end_header_id|>", turn_close="<|eot_id|>", think_open="<|start_think|>", think_close="<|end_think|>", ) # Qwen3 and Qwen3.5 share one convention, as does Nemotron-H apart from its BOS. QWEN_TOKENS = ChatTokens( bos="", turn_open_prefix="<|im_start|>", turn_open_suffix="", turn_close="<|im_end|>", think_open="", think_close="", ) NEMOTRON_TOKENS = ChatTokens( bos="", turn_open_prefix="<|im_start|>", turn_open_suffix="", turn_close="<|im_end|>", think_open="", think_close="", ) # Keys match the trainer-side architecture names (Axolotl's config strings; "grug" # for the Levanter Snowball path). FAMILY_TOKEN_MAPS: dict[str, ChatTokens] = { "grug": GRUG_TOKENS, "qwen3_moe": QWEN_TOKENS, "qwen3_5_moe": QWEN_TOKENS, "nemotron_h": NEMOTRON_TOKENS, } # Each family's pinned tokenizer, as (repo id, revision): the same tokenizers the # token maps are validated against, reused wherever a token-exact count is needed # (trace caps, mask lengths). The pins are the single canonical copy; Stage 0's # length filter reads them from here. FAMILY_TOKENIZER_REVISIONS: dict[str, tuple[str, str]] = { "grug": ("open-athena/snowball-67b-a2b-base-262k-qk175", "11c9430da3075ef4596f92ee0af142d9d08215c1"), "qwen3_moe": ("Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Base", "1b75feb79f60b8dc6c5bc769a898c206a1c6a4f9"), "qwen3_5_moe": ("Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-Base", "0f0813072d2358973511097385626f21fcb6d422"), "nemotron_h": ("nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-Base-BF16", "e0ac9ee3dfd02be21b5479edfc2f671ed269d0a2"), } def _jinja_literal(value: str) -> str: """Escape ``value`` for use inside a single-quoted Jinja string literal.""" return value.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace("'", "\\'").replace("\n", "\\n").replace("\r", "\\r") def shared_template(tokens: ChatTokens) -> str: """The shared Jinja template with one family's delimiters baked in as literals.""" template = _TEMPLATE_SKELETON for placeholder, value in ( (_BOS, tokens.bos), (_TURN_OPEN_PREFIX, tokens.turn_open_prefix), (_TURN_OPEN_SUFFIX, tokens.turn_open_suffix), (_TURN_CLOSE, tokens.turn_close), (_THINK_OPEN, tokens.think_open), (_THINK_CLOSE, tokens.think_close), ): template = template.replace(placeholder, _jinja_literal(value)) assert _TURN_OPEN_PREFIX not in template, "skeleton placeholders must all be baked" return template def template_sha256(tokens: ChatTokens) -> str: """The sha256 of the rendered template, for manifests and integrity checks.""" return hashlib.sha256(shared_template(tokens).encode()).hexdigest() def validate_token_map(tokens: ChatTokens, tokenizer) -> dict[str, int]: """Check every delimiter encodes to exactly one token of ``tokenizer``. Returns the token lengths by slot; raises ``ValueError`` naming the offending slot otherwise. ``bos`` is exempt when empty (Qwen has none). """ lengths: dict[str, int] = {} for slot in ("turn_open_prefix", "turn_open_suffix", "turn_close", "think_open", "think_close"): value = getattr(tokens, slot) if not value: continue length = len(tokenizer.encode(value, add_special_tokens=False)) if length != 1: raise ValueError(f"{slot}={value!r} encodes to {length} tokens; the shared template needs one") lengths[slot] = length if tokens.bos: bos_length = len(tokenizer.encode(tokens.bos, add_special_tokens=False)) if bos_length != 1: raise ValueError(f"bos={tokens.bos!r} encodes to {bos_length} tokens; the shared template needs one") lengths["bos"] = bos_length slots = [tokens.turn_open_prefix, tokens.turn_open_suffix, tokens.turn_close, tokens.think_open, tokens.think_close] non_empty = [slot for slot in slots if slot] if len(set(non_empty)) != len(non_empty): raise ValueError("token map delimiters must be distinct") return lengths ```
